stories.title: SEC staff posts a new interpretations index
stories.classification: Staff interpretations index · Not a Litecoin approval
stories.dek: The SEC’s October 15 update lists new or revised staff questions on filing-fee computation, compensatory offerings, Form S-8 and Form 4.
paragraphs: The SEC’s October 15 index lists new or revised staff questions on filing fees, compensatory offerings, Form S-8 and Form 4. This is a staff-interpretations update, not a new Litecoin rule or product approval.
The index links the underlying questions. Readers should consult those texts for their specific subject; this brief does not infer a legal outcome for a company, fund or token.
stories.takeaway: An updated staff interpretation and a Commission rulemaking are different records.
stories.discussionPrompt: Which disclosure term should our next source guide explain?

stories.title: A new checkpoint, with the dates left visible
stories.classification: Secondary compiled dataset · Not fund flows
stories.dek: Today’s distribution derivative uses September 16 as its 30-day baseline. Each row retains its actual observation date and any unknown baseline.
stories.status: Prepared October16 · Underlying row dates vary
paragraphs: The current derivative is prepared from Litecoin Register’s compiled records. It preserves zero balances, unknown earlier observations and the date of each eligible record.
Rows can overlap across entities or categories. The sum is a tracked-record total, not a count of unique coins, independently verified custody, or money newly invested during the period.
stories.takeaway: Read source dates before interpreting a change as a purchase.
stories.discussionPrompt: Which primary issuer record would improve this map?

stories.title: The halving clock is a model, not a promise
stories.dek: The timechain guide separates observed blocks, estimated halving time and scheduled issuance, with a source-linked merged-mining explanation.
stories.status: Current guide checked October16 · Educational context
paragraphs: The guide now refreshes provider-reported block observations and calculates a target-time halving estimate. A countdown does not predict the exact date a future block will arrive.

Scheduled issuance includes the mathematical subsidy from genesis; it is not an audit of spendable or circulating supply. The separate playground lets readers inspect the subsidy at exact halving boundaries.
Its merged-mining section distinguishes reusable work, independent ledgers and pool-specific payouts. Auxiliary rewards may help cover costs, but do not guarantee mining profitability.
stories.takeaway: Separate a protocol schedule from a market prediction.
stories.discussionPrompt: Which part of merged mining needs a diagram next?
